restrictions: Two distinct 128-byte one-block messages m(a), m(b) of sha3-256-r6-prefix-v1 (zero state, rate 136, suffix 0x06 with pad10*1, rounds 0 to 5, full 256-bit digest). m(u) places the point u (lanes u0..u3) in lanes 1, 6, 11 = u0, u1, u0^u1^K11 and 4, 9, 14 = u2, u3, u2^u3^K14, the other lanes 0..15 fixed constants K (proof.md Section 2); m is injective. F(u) = digest of m(u) xor a fixed mask PD; F(a) = F(b) with a != b is an ordinary collision. Round 0 and round-1 theta are affine in u (a Guo-Liu-Song 2016 linear structure).

Distinguished-point parallel collision search (van Oorschot-Wiener) on F with 256 walks per step, as in our entry 2d74a370: DP = 116 top bits of F zero, cap Lc = 2^120 - 2 steps, at most 5,000 trails and a table of 5,000 words, Tb = 17750576 x 2^96 steps, a prefilter-hit counter that aborts the attempt at hit HMAX + 1 (HMAX = floor(Tb (1 + 2^-20)/2^8) + 1 + Lc), one replay with a one-walk program of F of 1,115 operations (proof.md Section 4).

Machine (declared heuristic H_machine): a register file of 1,024 words of 256 bits (1,018 for program values, 6 for the loop state), every load, store and register move is an instruction charged as one word operation, code counted at 32 bytes per instruction, no compact encoding and no interpreter. One step of 256 walks is 36,878 operations: sections AFF 3,081, GB 8,063 and GA 8,500 (each run twice, shared code), R5 637, with 6,885 loads, stores and moves of the allocation, plus loop 14, prefilter 17, counter 3 (Section 3).

Cost model collision-frontier-v5, unit 1626: N = Tb x 36,878 + (2 x 1,115 + 26) x Lc + R + PRE = 55143574691449961658368535021444063567770 word operations, every loop-control, test, transfer and handler operation counted, at most HMAX + 1 prefilter hits at 211 each in every execution (Section 4); time_log2 = 124.67321 = log2(N/1626) rounded up, integer certificate 1626^100000 2^12467320 < N^100000 <= 1626^100000 2^12467321 (Appendix A).

Preprocessing, run by the attack and charged in N: the constant-selection run gen 512 (512 candidate constant sets, Appendix C), 513 x 2^32 + 512 x 2^10 operations, and the generator gen_s6ls (Appendix B), which selects the polarity pattern over all 2^25 patterns and the boundary size over 7 sizes and writes the program, 2^34 operations (measured 2^33.85 executed instructions); PRE = 2,220,498,616,320, preprocessing_log2 31. No advice.

Memory at most 1,032,320 bytes <= 2^20 (register file, program code at 32 bytes per instruction, other code, spill cells, table, walk state; Section 6). The two preprocessing programs run before the search: measured peaks (VmHWM, whole static image counted) 552,960 bytes for gen 512 and 1,032,192 bytes for gen_s6ls including the code region it writes; both also fit a 1 MiB sandbox that counts the declared span. memory_log2_bytes = 20; the Python experiments (about 86 MB) are reduced-width evidence, not the attack.

Success at least 0.39 for one attempt over the fresh word rho, under the score-critical premise H_rand (F behaves as a random function on the evaluated points), with failure terms for cut trails, table limit, self-coincidence, starts and key matches, and the hit-counter abort F5 < 2^-1000 proved by a Chernoff bound (Section 5). No full-scale run and no full collision is claimed.

heuristics.statement: F(u) = SHA3-256-r6(m(u)) xor PD, with the linear-structure message embedding m of proof.md Section 2, behaves as a uniformly random function from 256-bit values to 256-bit values on the points the search evaluates: values at distinct inputs are independent and uniform, a fresh point is a distinguished point with probability 2^-116, and the remaining length of a trail after a coincidence is geometric with parameter 2^-116 independently of the time of the coincidence. Then the first image coincidence among e evaluations has probability at least 1 - exp(-e(e-1)/2^257), and one attempt succeeds with probability at least 0.39 after the failure terms of proof.md Section 5.
heuristics.scope: The fixed function F of proof.md Section 2 on the points of one attempt: about 1.058 x 2^128 evaluations in 256 lockstep walks from starts rho + i, i < 5,000. Only the pair-coincidence rate among evaluated images and the distinguished-point rate enter the bound. The step program, the cost, the memory and the failure terms are derived, not assumed.
heuristics.extrapolation: Organizer-executed: rho-w22 runs the whole search with the claimed program at width 22 (every trial must return a 22-bit partial collision; our 1,280 local trials took 18.29 steps on average against 17.94 for an ideal random function, z = +1.8); proj-w256 runs eight chained full-width steps and tests 22-bit agreement among 2,048 iterates (model 0.3934 per trial; our local 490/1,280). Our own C runs on this F (proof.md Section 7.2): pair-coincidence rates on three 32-bit windows among 2^24 images of uniform inputs, of the starts rho + i and of chained iterates are within 0.6 percent of the random value; single-bit differences show no bias (max |z| 4.09 over 65,536 cells); the proj trial at scale gives 0.3938 in 262,144 trials; GPU rho lengths of truncated chains at 32, 36 and 40 bits have pooled mean ratios 0.998, 1.003 and 1.008 to the random value (4 and 3 seeds at 36 and 40 bits; one 36-bit run read 1.027). Extrapolated from 22- to 40-bit projections to 256-bit coincidences at 2^128 evaluations.
heuristics.limitations: An assumption, not proved. The affine round 0 leaves five nonlinear rounds; a structural deviation of the collision rate at 256 bits that does not appear in the projections is not excluded. If the pair-coincidence rate is (1 - eps) of uniform, the same success costs about 0.5 log2(1/(1 - eps)) more bits (0.0073 for eps = 0.01).

heuristics.statement: The 256-bit word RAM of collision-frontier-v5 is taken with a register file of 1,024 words of 256 bits (1,018 hold program values, 6 the loop state), counted as memory (32,768 bytes). Every load, store and register-to-register move is an instruction and is charged as one word operation in every routine; no memory word is read or written except by a charged load or store. All code is counted at 32 bytes per instruction; there is no compact encoding, interpreter or decode convention (proof.md Section 3.2).
heuristics.scope: The machine that runs the step program and the search of proof.md Section 4; it fixes the time and memory ledgers, not the success bound.
heuristics.extrapolation: The cost model and the target profile fix no register count; this is the convention under which our blake3-r3 entry 0a9640ed was accepted (1,024-word register file, all transfers charged everywhere). Every transfer the program needs is written in the program (6,885 loads, stores and moves per step) and counted; the executed checks validate the function of this program, and the counts are those of the generated listing (Appendix B).
heuristics.limitations: A declared convention, not a measured property of hardware. With a larger file and no transfers the same sections give 124.38871 (not claimed); without shared code or with all planes in memory at section boundaries the cost is higher (proof.md Section 8).
